why: The first turn under ADR 0049, and deliberately a configuration whose answer is already known. Seeds 1, 2 and 3 at lambda 0.9 with the ADR 0048 baseline are exactly ci-88, ci-90 and ci-91, which ran one at a time and scored 0.6625, 0.0975 and 0.30375 against search-4, 0.0325, 0.15375 and 0.03375 against Greedy, and 0.725, 0.79875 and 0.82125 for the clone against Greedy. So this run is a regression test of the new multi-seed loop as much as an experiment: the spread it prints must reproduce those nine numbers to the digit, because nothing about the training or the evaluation changed -- only that the turn now runs all three seeds itself, reports the range, and makes the gate require every seed. If a number moves, the refactor moved it and that is a bug, not a finding. What to read: spread.json, specifically the width column. The value policy's width against search-4 should come out near 0.565, which is the measurement that ADR 0049 is built on -- a spread from the dataset seed alone that is larger than every effect this project has measured. Expect nothing to be committed: the clone's minimum against Greedy is 0.725 and it must also measurably beat the champion ci-69 on every seed, which ci-91 did not do (0.42375, interval from 0.387). Next after this, and only once the machinery is trusted: re-measure ADR 0048's baseline fix as a spread rather than as the single seed it was reported on, since its 19-point win-rate gain is inside this width and was withdrawn.
